addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- integration-api-validator: Validates an external integration's API before any code is written. Characterizes transport, auth, pagination, response format, token refresh, and webhook style; identifies the closest existing integration as exemplar via parallel Explore searches. Use when starting a new integration via /plan-integration, or ad-hoc to re-characterize an existing integration whose source API has changed (vendor migration, new endpoints, deprecation). Outputs `.claude/references/{name}/api-summary.md`. (Tools: Bash, Read, Write, WebFetch, Grep, Glob)

- integration-data-seeder: Seeds a vendor's writes-safe sandbox with enough test data for downstream function-writer validation — products, inventory, orders distributed across states, returns, inbound shipments — and attempts state transitions (ship, cancel, process). Records under api-summary.md "Sandbox seeding" what was created and any state transitions that couldn't be driven via API (vendor UI required, real carrier needed, etc.). Spawned by the orchestrator after `integration-api-validator` finishes characterization, when the validator's reads turned up a thin or empty sandbox. Single-pass agent — runs once per integration build. (Tools: Bash, Read, Write, WebFetch, Grep, Glob)

- integration-function-writer: Implements one coherent unit of integration code — either a single data function (get_orders, get_inventory, write_order, etc.) or the auth bundle (get_integration_secret + <name>_request + validate_integration_secret). Iterates with yarn crawl + yarn test until validated. Standard path is via /plan-integration after the api-validator has produced api-summary.md. Can also be invoked ad-hoc for a single-method add to an existing integration when the exemplar is already known. Adheres strictly to .claude/references/integration-patterns.md. (Tools: Read, Edit, Write, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- integration-reviewer: Reviews a single unit of integration code (one data function, the auth bundle, or a single test file) against `.claude/references/integration-patterns.md`. Pattern-matches against the exemplar from api-summary.md when present. Runs targeted `yarn test`. Emits a structured BLOCK / APPROVE / APPROVE_WITH_NOTES verdict. Has no edit access — surfaces findings only. Use after each integration-function-writer invocation in /plan-integration, OR ad-hoc to review a single file or diff when debugging an integration, investigating a customer issue, or pre-PR. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- agent-pylon-investigate: Autonomous Pylon-ticket investigator for an unattended cloud routine. Fired once per new ticket by a Pylon webhook. Triage (skip noise / route non-technical / investigate) → check prior art → wrap the `investigate` skill → post a Pylon INTERNAL NOTE, and open a draft PR for a clear fix to the reported bug. Unrelated bugs found along the way become Linear cards, not PRs. Fully unattended, internal-only. Use when handed a Pylon issue id (UUID) in a routine session.
- bulk-resync: Bulk resync connections for a given org and integration. Queries DynamoDB for connection IDs and runs the resync script.
- configure-schedule: Adjust crawl schedules for connections by modifying DynamoDB scheduler rows
- create-linear-issue: The one surface that creates a Linear issue. Two modes — compose a card from a freeform human ask (pick the Type label + integration/customer label, write a short human body), or file a caller-supplied spec verbatim (used by automated skills like stale-schedule-investigate, which own their own title grammar and labels). Always reads the live workspace label set and never invents labels. Use when asked to file/create/open a Linear issue, ticket, or card, and whenever another skill needs to create one. Out of scope: editing or closing existing issues.
- distill: Weekly consolidation pass over the .claude/ markdown — compact api-summary files to current API behavior, promote patterns humans taught via PR review into gotchas / rules / CLAUDE.md, and fix skill instructions whose output humans corrected on review. Use for the scheduled distillation routine or ad hoc when knowledge files have drifted into append-only history (`/distill [--lookback <days>]`). Markdown only: no code edits; the deliverable is a single draft PR.
- fan-out-change: Make one change ripple correctly across every integration (or every file in a large set) — a new canonical field, a renamed helper, a formatter-shape change, a signature migration. Use when a single schema/infra edit forces a matching edit in dozens or hundreds of `integrations/**/integration.py` files and each site needs per-integration judgment (real value vs IntegrationNotImplemented, docs-first surfacing, FOLLOW-UP when unverifiable) rather than a blind find-replace. Fan out by file/integration, each agent owning a slice; verify structurally before trusting any "done".
- fix-tests: Analyze failing tests from the daily CI report (Slack), a GitHub Actions run, or pasted yarn test output and implement root-cause fixes — both integration tests (live vendor crawls in test/integrations) and non-integration tests (api / celery / lambda / utils / transports). Use when asked to fix failing tests, work the daily CI failure report, or when given pytest failures. Every failure is reproduced and classified before any edit — never a green-at-any-cost shortcut like ignoring validation, weakening an assert, or skipping.
- integration-pr: Create or refresh a pokedex integration PR — body and field-mapping comment. Default behavior is create-from-current-branch; positional PR URL / `#NN` switches to refresh mode (detect-and-patch the existing body + mapping comment). Triggered by `/integration-pr [<pr>]`, or invoked via Skill() by `/wrap-integration` step 8 and `/plan-integration` finalize — the canonical PR-creation surface for orchestrating skills. Only for integration PRs — never invoke for a non-integration branch, and never auto-invoke from prose that merely mentions opening a PR.
- inventory-mapping: Build an inventory field-mapping breakdown — how each canonical Trackstar inventory field (awaiting/onhand/committed/unfulfillable/fulfillable/sellable) is derived from a given WMS integration's source fields. Use when a customer or ticket asks how Trackstar inventory fields map to the underlying integration.
- investigate: Investigate Trackstar integration issues — missing data, field mismatches, webhook failures, sync delays, stale schedules, crawl errors, credential problems, and customer-reported bugs. Use when debugging any connection issue, when a customer reports data problems, when schedules are stale, when analyzing Datadog error logs, or when triaging a support thread. Always use this skill for any Trackstar investigation, even if the issue type isn't immediately clear.
- pylon: Fetch Pylon issues, read messages, and post private (internal) notes via the Pylon REST API. Use when looking up a Pylon ticket by id, reading its message thread, or adding an internal note. Replaces the pylon MCP tools.
- query-datadog: How to query Datadog logs for Trackstar crawler investigations — the tags-vs-attributes distinction, the standard crawler log query for a connection / integration / function, pinning the time window to the staleness range, and building shareable Datadog links for PRs and Linear cards. Use whenever querying Datadog for a stale schedule, crawl error, sync issue, or any connection problem.
- review-code: Review integration code for quality, pattern adherence, and production readiness before merging
- run-scripts: Canonical invocations for the pokedex yarn scripts (yarn test, yarn crawl, yarn curl, yarn serve, yarn generate, yarn install-integration, yarn worker). Use whenever about to run tests, invoke pytest, exercise an integration method, scaffold a new integration, push dev credentials, or hit the local Pokedex API. **Required reading before running any tests** — never invoke `python -m pytest` or `pytest` directly; always use `yarn test` with the right filters.
- scrape-docs: Scrape and process API documentation from URLs, PDFs, or OpenAPI specs into LLM-optimized markdown
- se-investigate: Solutions-Engineer front door for a Pylon ticket. Triage (skip noise / route non-technical / investigate), check if we've already answered it (Slack + past Pylon tickets), run the investigation, then post findings as a Pylon INTERNAL NOTE. Use when handed a Pylon ticket id to investigate end-to-end. Runs unattended (a local poller opens a session per new ticket - see https://github.com/trackstarhq/pylon-dispatcher).
- stale-schedule-dispatch: Triage stale Trackstar crawl schedules and fan out one investigation per root-cause cluster. Use to run the stale-schedule dispatcher (scheduled routine or ad hoc) — pull the stale set, drop what shouldn't be worked on, dedup against in-flight investigations via the scheduler-row pointer, cluster by root cause, and fire one investigator per cluster. Read-only: no code edits, no PRs, no DynamoDB writes.
- stale-schedule-investigate: Diagnose the root cause of one stale Trackstar crawl-schedule cluster and either ship a tested fix as a PR or escalate with evidence. Use when handed a stale-schedule cluster (the dispatcher's /fire payload, or ad hoc) — investigate root cause, open the Linear issue, write the investigation pointer to the scheduler rows, then act per classification (code fix + PR, or escalate / customer / vendor / infra). Composes the read-only `investigate` skill for diagnosis.
- update-crawl-frequency: Update crawl_frequencies on a connection to change how often specific flows sync
- validate-api: Validate API behavior before implementation by testing auth, collecting samples, and documenting discrepancies
- catchup: Catchup - Review Branch Changes
- debug-report: Debug Report - Investigate Customer Issues
- diagram-trackstar: Regenerate the Trackstar architecture diagrams in docs/architecture/, grounded in real code
- generate-support-email: Generate Support Email - Draft Email to WMS/API Vendor
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch
